greyCapBlocks.text: Nothing on this screen is made up. A panel that could not be loaded says so and stays empty. It never keeps rows from an earlier load, and it never stands in numbers of its own.
These are counts of real rows, not scores. Clicking a tile filters the panel it came from and jumps to it.

This is our own copy of today's spend, not the ad platform's. A green row is not proof that spend is under control — it only means our copy looks fine. The breached flag is the one that reads the ad platform directly, so it stays right even when our copy is behind.

Do not add these rows up. A partner limit, a platform limit and a campaign limit can all count the same money. Headroom never goes below zero — an overspend shows up as a percentage above 100 instead.

0 of 0 campaigns have no daily limit of their own and so appear nowhere above. They are still covered by the partner and platform limits. Once a limit has been breached, every further budget change is refused until a person clears it.

Spend here is yesterday's, on purpose. Today's is only part of a day, and a list judged on it makes a campaign that started at 11pm look dead. Today's spend is in the panel above, and only per limit — there is no today's figure for a single campaign.

Status is the ad platform's own word for the campaign and Synced is when we last pulled it in. Both stay empty until Sync Meta now fills them. There is no link out to Ads Manager: nothing here holds the campaign's id on the ad platform.

The recommendation is the optimiser's, not this screen's. It sends back one word — refresh, queue, ok, or unconfigured — and nothing here adds to it. Unconfigured means both of the optimiser's creative rules are switched off for this partner, so it is all-or-nothing across the whole table, never a verdict on one ad.

An ad missing from this table is not a healthy ad. Only ads with activity in the window are listed at all. The figures are plain day-by-day averages, not weighted by how much each day was shown. There is no fatigue score and no picture of the creative.

Whether a campaign may go live is decided by the system, not on this screen. The connection has to be active and the business verified. Verifying a business is done in the ad platform's own Business Manager — there is nothing to click here, and nothing here connects an account.
No password or access key is ever shown here — only whether one is stored and when it runs out. A blank expiry means we do not know, not "valid forever".

A blocker is raised for one campaign but listed against the connection, so the same blocker can appear more than once. Which campaign it came from is not part of this list, so this screen does not name one. A Google connection can be read here but not changed from here.

There are four outcomes and no others: done, failed, undone, or written down but never carried out. There is no "pending" and no "retrying" — nothing here tries a second time, so a row that says it was never carried out will stay that way.

Every kill switch row says "never carried out" — that is how it is written down, not what happened. The stop itself did happen: the limit was flagged as breached and the campaigns under it were paused. Ad sets underneath keep the state they had.

The row is written before the change is sent, then stamped when it comes back. That is why "written down but never carried out" is a state you can find rather than a change that vanished. Nothing in this list can be edited or deleted.

"Revertible" is a flag, not a button. Nothing on this screen can undo an action. Rows from the optimiser usually carry no name — the rule is the attribution. Names on human rows are the partner's own users.
